summary: Walker County, AL 100-foot CCC steel tower built about 1941 and removed by 1960; its foundations were moved and now serve as gateposts to a property.

facts.design: 100' steel tower built by the CCC
facts.status_note: Removed by 1960; the foundations were taken from their original location and now serve as gateposts to the property. No source describes what remains at the original site.
facts.agency: Private owner (register names an individual administrator)

access.note: Register names a private administrator; the relocated foundations serve as gateposts to the property; no public access described

notes_for_editor: Two sources. The register gives the tower's dates only approximately ('circa 1941', 'before 1960'), so the brief's 1941 and 1960 event years are rounded from those phrases. The MountainZone page gives the summit's approximate elevation as 784 ft (239 m), against the register's 794 ft (242 m) for the lookout; these measure different points, so it is not treated as a conflict. The summit coordinates match the register's to within about 20 m, which is why the story can place the site near Carbon Hill. The register names a private administrator; the name is kept out of the story. No new photos added: the register page's photo of the relocated footers (courtesy of Andrew Zerbe) is already on the page. Relocation has no year in any source, so no 'relocated' event is recorded. No corrections proposed.
